topic: SC: in accident claims, functional disability can exceed the medical board's percentage - a victim who needs a lifelong attendant can be treated as 100% functionally disabled; higher attendant charges (Sunil Kumar v. IFFCO Tokio General Insurance, 2026 INSC 1145)

slides.title: Accident victim? Disability is more than a **number**
slides.subtitle: If a victim needs an attendant for life, the loss can be counted as **100%**, even if the medical board said less.
slides.cite: **Sunil Kumar v. IFFCO Tokio General Insurance Co. Ltd.**, 2026 INSC 1145 · Justices S.V.N. Bhatti and N.V. Anjaria

slides.label: The case
slides.title: A scooter crash in **2016**
bullets: A 43-year-old man riding pillion on a scooter suffered **severe head and brain injuries** in a road accident.
He now needs **someone to look after him for the rest of his life**.
The medical board put his disability at **75.5%**. The High Court went by that figure.

slides.label: What the court said
slides.title: Look at **real life**, not just the certificate
bullets: **Medical disability** is the injury as certified by doctors. **Functional disability** is how much it affects daily life and work.
Functional disability can be **higher** than the medical percentage.
A person who needs an attendant for life cannot work at all, so his loss of earning capacity is **100%**.
slides.note: **Law fact:** Courts must give **realistic** compensation, looking at how much the victim could have earned.

slides.label: The result
slides.title: Compensation **more than doubled**
bullets: Total award raised to about **₹77.84 lakh** (High Court had given ₹36.22 lakh). Attendant charges went up from ₹1 lakh to **₹25.20 lakh**.
The scooter driver, also injured, was assessed at **80%** functional disability against a medical **62%**.
The extra amount carries **6.5% interest** and must be deposited within **six weeks**.

slides.label: Keep in mind
slides.title: Every case is **different**
bullets: This does **not** mean every injury counts as 100%. The court looks at the facts and how the injury affects that person's work.
Keep medical records, bills and proof of income safe. They help the tribunal assess the true loss.
This post is for information only, not legal advice.

caption:
A disability certificate does not tell the whole story, says the Supreme Court 🚑⚖️

A 43-year-old man suffered severe head and brain injuries in a scooter accident in 2016. He now needs an attendant for the rest of his life. The medical board rated his disability at 75.5%, and the High Court calculated compensation on that basis.

The Supreme Court explained the difference between medical disability (the injury doctors certify) and functional disability (how much the injury affects a person's daily life and work). Functional disability can be higher than the medical figure. Since this man cannot do his own work, let alone earn, the court treated his loss of earning capacity as 100%. Courts must give realistic compensation based on what the victim could have earned.

The court raised his total award to about ₹77.84 lakh, against ₹36.22 lakh given by the High Court, and increased attendant charges from ₹1 lakh to ₹25.20 lakh. The injured scooter driver was assessed at 80% functional disability against a medical 62%. The extra amounts carry 6.5% yearly interest and the insurer must deposit them within six weeks. This does not mean every injury is 100%; each case depends on its facts.

Case: Sunil Kumar (Totally Disabled, Represented by Wife) v. IFFCO Tokio General Insurance Company Limited, 2026 INSC 1145
Bench: Justices S.V.N. Bhatti and N.V. Anjaria, Supreme Court of India
